skill.name: haskell-pro
skill.description: Expert Haskell engineer specializing in advanced type systems, pure functional design, and high-reliability software. Use PROACTIVELY for type-level programming, concurrency, and architecture guidance.
skill.summary: Advanced Haskell guidance for type-safe architecture, concurrency, performance, and testing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by a markdown file path wrapped in backticks. I found no evidence of command execution, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 25 only references `resources/implementation-playbook.md` as a markdown file path. It is not executable code and provides no shell invocation or command injection vector.

content.value_statement: Haskell projects can be hard to design, test, and tune safely. This skill provides expert guidance for type-driven design, concurrency, parsing, performance, and maintainable architecture.
actual_capabilities: Designs Haskell modules with explicit types, newtypes, and domain invariants.
Explains advanced type system tools such as GADTs, type families, and phantom types.
Recommends concurrency patterns using STM, async, and exception-safe boundaries.
Improves parsing and JSON workflows with Megaparsec and Aeson guidance.
Suggests QuickCheck and Hspec tests for property-based validation.
Reviews Cabal or Stack structure, dependency hygiene, and performance concerns.
limitations: It gives guidance and examples, but does not execute builds or tests by itself.
It needs project context before recommending language extensions or abstractions.
It may require tool output from GHC, Cabal, Stack, or profilers for precise diagnosis.
It does not replace security or production readiness review for deployed systems.

use_cases.title: Model Domain Invariants
use_cases.description: Convert fragile data shapes into stronger Haskell types with clear constructors and safer APIs.

use_cases.title: Review Concurrent Code
use_cases.description: Evaluate STM, async, and exception handling choices for safer concurrent Haskell services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Advanced Haskell Lessons
use_cases.description: Create explanations and exercises for GADTs, typeclasses, parsing, and property testing.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Haskell Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Haskell concept in simple terms, then show when I should use it: [concept].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Module Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Haskell module for stronger types, safer functions, and clearer boundaries: [module summary].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Haskell workflow for [domain task] using explicit types, validation, and testable pure functions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Reliability and Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Haskell service design for concurrency risks, strictness issues, parsing errors, and missing property tests: [context].

output_examples.input: Review a payment state model that uses strings for every status.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a closed sum type for payment states, smart constructors for validated transitions, and property tests for invalid paths.

output_examples.input: Improve a parser that returns unclear errors.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest Megaparsec error bundles, smaller parser combinators, named labels, and tests covering valid and invalid input.

output_examples.input: Check a service that mixes database IO with business rules.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate pure decision logic from effectful boundaries, add explicit result types, and propose tests for the pure layer.

best_practices: Share relevant type definitions, module boundaries, and compiler errors with each request.
Ask for the smallest useful abstraction before adding advanced type system features.
Verify recommendations with GHC, tests, and profiler output when performance matters.
anti_patterns: Do not request advanced extensions without explaining the practical problem.
Do not hide partial functions, runtime exceptions, or unsafe IO inside pure-looking APIs.
Do not treat generated examples as production code without review and tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, review, and explain Haskell code using strong types, pure functions, concurrency tools, and tests.

faq.question: Can it debug compiler errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the error message, relevant types, and module context for the best guidance.

faq.question: Does it write full applications?
faq.answer: It can outline modules and provide examples, but complete applications need project-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Is it only for advanced Haskell users?
faq.answer: No. It can explain beginner topics, then scale to advanced type systems and production architecture.

faq.question: Can it improve performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest strictness, profiling, fusion, and data structure changes when enough context is available.

faq.question: Does it support Cabal and Stack?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review project structure, dependencies, build configuration, and module organization for both tools.
